from_quote: the article in the new Constitution, which says that treaties shall be paramount to the laws of the land
rationale: The speaker names "the article in the new Constitution" making treaties paramount to the laws of the land; he gives no number and does not quote it.
to_quote: all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States, shall be the supreme Law of the Land

from_quote: the President has power, with advice and consent of the Senate, to make treaties, provided two thirds of the Senate present concur
rationale: The paragraph states the treaty-making clause almost in its words.
to_quote: by and with the Advice and Consent of the Senate, to make Treaties, provided two thirds of the Senators present concur

from_quote: removed from office on impeachment and conviction of treason, bribery, or other high crimes and misdemeanors
rationale: Pinckney lists the President, Vice-President and civil officers as removable on impeachment and conviction, in the clause's words.
to_quote: removed from Office on Impeachment for, and Conviction of, Treason, Bribery, or other high Crimes and Misdemeanors

from_quote: the clause relative to the negroes
rationale: Barnwell calls it "the clause relative to the negroes" and says the United States shall not consider the matter for twenty-one years; it does not quote the clause.
to_quote: shall not be prohibited by the Congress prior to the Year one thousand eight hundred and eight
